citation: Ferrari, S. L. P. and Cribari-Neto, F. (2004), Beta Regression for Modelling Rates and Proportions, Journal of Applied Statistics 31(7), 799-815, DOI 10.1080/0266476042000214501 -- Table 2, `Parameter estimates using data on food expenditure`, whose four rows print beta1 -0.62255, beta2 -0.01230, beta3 0.11846 and phi 35.60975 for a logit-link beta regression of the share of household income spent on food on income and household size, over the 38 households of Griffiths, Hill and Judge (1993), Table 15.4.
notes:
THE PAYLOAD'S ONE PUBLISHED NUMBER IS phi, AND params IS UNCLAIMABLE FOR A REASON THAT HAS NOTHING TO DO WITH PRECISION. `numerically_equal` compares a mapping on its whole key set and RECURSES: `unchecked_keys` exempts a TOP-LEVEL field only, so naming `params` in `expected` claims all three terms times all six statistics -- estimate, std_error, z_value, p_value, conf_low and conf_high. Table 2 publishes the estimates and the standard errors and nothing else, and the standard errors are the ones this payload cannot carry: they come from the EXPECTED information matrix, the closed-form W following the paper's equation (9), while `BetaResults` is a GenericLikelihoodModel whose `bse` inverts the OBSERVED numerical Hessian. MEASURED against statsmodels 0.14.6 on the committed fixtures: the page prints 0.22385, 0.00304 and 0.03534 and the body returns 0.22137, 0.00308 and 0.03574 -- a disagreement of about 1.1e-02 relative at worst, nine hundred times outside `estimate-1e-4` and outside every class _policy.json defines. Reproducing the published pair means implementing the expected information in this engine and reporting it in place of the value the library gives, which is a much larger change than this method. So `params` is unchecked whatever else is true of it, and a test pins the observed-against-expected gap so that a release which moves it is visible.

THE SECOND REASON, WHICH WOULD BIND ON ITS OWN IF THE FIRST DID NOT. Even the estimates alone could not be claimed at this class. MEASURED, read back from the body on the committed fixtures: the intercept agrees with the page at 1.33e-06 relative, `persons` at 1.84e-05, and `income` at 9.54e-05 -- inside `estimate-1e-4`, and only just. The page prints that coefficient as -0.01230, five decimal places over a number of size 0.0123, so the ROUNDING FLOOR of the printed digit alone is 5e-6/0.0123 = 4.07e-04 relative: four times wider than the band the class allows. The comparison is satisfiable only because the true value happened to fall in the inner quarter of the printed interval, and the slack left is 5.7e-08 in absolute terms -- 4.6e-06 of the estimate, which is the scale of a convergence tolerance. `estimate-1e-4` is named for the convergence criterion setting the floor, and here a change of that size in the optimiser would turn the case red without anything being wrong. Reaching for `pvalue-1e-3` to widen the band is refused for the reason the sibling case under count_models/ refuses it: the class describes a p-value compared near zero and would describe neither the number nor the reason. MEASURED rather than assumed about the loader: `pvalue-1e-3` and `statistic-1e-6` both BITE on this payload and would both be admitted at load time, so nothing in the harness would have stopped either -- the choice is this file's own and is semantic.

WHERE THE PUBLISHED COEFFICIENTS ARE COMPARED INSTEAD, because they are not left unexamined. `ld_fractional_response`'s docstring carries an executable example that rounds all three to the five decimals Table 2 prints and reproduces -0.62255, -0.0123 and 0.11846 exactly; `run_verifications.sh` step 11 RUNS it, so that comparison is a gate rather than a comment. It is the honest comparison at the precision the source supports, and it lives in exactly one place.

WHY phi CAN BE CHECKED WHEN THE COEFFICIENTS CANNOT. It is printed as 35.60975 -- seven significant figures, a rounding floor of 1.4e-07 -- and the body returns 35.60973310373236, which is 4.74e-07 relative from the page and 211 times inside the class. The disagreement is larger than the printing floor, so it is a real difference between two optimisers rather than an artefact of the digits, and it is three orders of magnitude smaller than the class allows for one.

WHY estimate-1e-4 AND NOT statistic-1e-6. phi comes out of a quasi-Newton search over the beta log-likelihood rather than from a closed form, which is what the class is for; the agreement would clear `statistic-1e-6` as well, and naming that class would describe the number wrongly. The perturbation control bites either way -- MEASURED: ten times this class's tolerance moves 35.60975 to 35.64535975, which the comparison refuses.

WHAT THIS CASE DOES NOT CLAIM BEYOND THAT. The paper's pseudo R-squared of 0.3878 is not a payload field, and `BetaResults.prsquared` returns 0.4088201409696193 under a definition that was not checked against theirs. `marginal_effects` has no published counterpart at all: the paper reports coefficients on the link scale and prints no effect on the proportion scale. `boundary_share` is 0.0 because no household in the table spends nothing or everything on food, which is what made a beta regression admissible here in the first place.
